content: Good medicine tastes bitter to the tongue, yet it cures the sickness; faithful counsel sounds harsh to the ear, yet it rectifies the life.
author: Chinese Proverbs
sourceWork: Liang yao ku kou, zhong yan ni er (良药苦口，忠言逆耳) — Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian)
explanation: Flattery is sweet sugar that rots the teeth and poisons the bloodstream. True friends and wise mentors do not tell you what flatters your fragile ego; they tell you the stinging truth that saves your life. Treasure the person who loves you enough to speak the bitter cure.
practicalInsight: When someone offers you critical feedback today, swallow your defensive pride. Reflect on what part of that bitter tonic is true.
reflectionPrompt: Who in your life gives you honest, unvarnished truth, and have you been punishing them for their courage?
